requested_parts: ordinary Repeat speed after explicitly made Slow
answers.answer: An ordinary Repeat uses the Power’s most recently assigned speed, so after it is explicitly made Slow, the Repeat occurs in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately follows its explicit timing directly after the originating use.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

requested_parts: measuring Range through Ocean during Ocean In Play
whether all outside edges become Coastal
answers.answer: Powers and Special Rules may measure Range through Ocean as a land on a board where Ocean is in play. This does not make every outside-edge land Coastal; only lands touching a printed Ocean are Coastal.

evidence.text: Each balanced board has eight lands, two each of Jungle, Mountain, Sands and Wetland. Lands are adjacent if they touch by border **or corner**, including across boards. Ocean is not normally a land or in play. Only lands touching a printed Ocean are Coastal; the other outside edges are cliffs, not coast. Other lands are Inland.

- **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). requested_parts: whether Damage boost can count for destruction Fear
answers.answer: No. One Damage does not destroy a healthy Town (Health 2) or City (Health 3). If a Damage boost causes the Power’s Damage to actually destroy a building, that destruction counts for its Fear; Damage boosts belong to the original Power when counting what it destroyed.

evidence.text:
| Piece | Health | Ravage Damage | Fear on destruction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Explorer | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Town | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| City | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| Dahan | 2 | 2 in counterattack | 0 |

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

- **Reading choices and Damage:** In **Crops Wither and Fade**, always gain 2 Fear before the City-or-Town replacement choice; “or” only divides adjacent clauses. **Veil the Night's Hunt** must put each point on a different Invader, wasting excess when there are fewer Invaders than Dahan. An unqualified “+N Damage” threshold adds total Damage at that step, not N to every previously damaged piece. Damage boosts still belong to the original Power when it counts what it destroyed.
